units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Brussels. I'm Anna.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And I'm Ben. And I'll admit, I've been looking forward to this one.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Why? It's the city with the waffles and the... what is it, the European Union?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Ha. Yes. The waffles and the European Union.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Which is a funny pairing, when you think about it.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Is it?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Well, one city has a Gothic town hall, a glass tower full of EU officials, a medieval square that was rebuilt in four years after a bombardment, and a whole boulevard built right on top of a river.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Wait. A river?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A river. We'll get there.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And I've heard it's a city where every street sign is in two languages.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Two languages on the signs, and nearly four in ten residents hold a foreign passport.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Four in ten. That's a lot.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It is. So here's what I want to know.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: How does a small town on a muddy river end up as the working capital of Europe?

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Trade, I'm guessing.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Trade. Guilds. Dukes. Emperors.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Revolutionaries.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Revolutionaries.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And a great deal of stubbornness.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Right, well, I'm sold. Where do we start?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: With the mud, naturally.
